## The question

[Using simple, MathJax-compatible TeX to put enclose a matrix in braces](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/102198/using-simple-mathjax-compatible-tex-to-put-enclose-a-matrix-in-braces), asked by [Alexander Gruber](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/6537/alexander-gruber) on TeX Stack Exchange (2013-03-12; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I was trying to explain the identity matrix over at [Math StackExchange][q-1] and I wound up using the following.
>
> ```latex
> $${\bf I_n} = \underbrace{
>                 \left.\left( 
>                       \begin{array}{ccccc}
>                              1&0&0&\cdots &0\\
>                              0&1&0&\cdots &0\\
>                              0&0&1&\cdots &0\\
>                              \vdots&&&\ddots&\\
>                              0&0&0&\cdots &1
>                       \end{array}
>                 \right)\right\}
>               }_{n\text{ columns}} 
>               \,n\text{ rows}
> $$
> ```
>
> It came out alright, but not quite what I wanted:
>
> ![Identity Matrix][q-2]
>
> I'd like to be able to move the ends of the underbrace inside the parenthesis without having it turn into this:
>
> ![Identity Matrix 2][q-3]
>
> Now, I see there are a couple of similar questions on here (examples: [1][q-4] [2][q-5]) which deal with the same issue.  However, all of them use a bunch of fancy stuff which I can't use in online forum TeX.
>
> > Is there a way to enclose a matrix in braces using only commands available in MathJax?
>
> I am not sure exactly which commands these are, but I am guessing a good rule of thumb would be the simplest commands possible.
>
>   [q-1]: https://math.stackexchange.com/a/328853/12952
>   [q-2]: LJdGA.png
>   [q-3]: fDRuA.png
>   [q-4]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/48572/6537
>   [q-5]: https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/44330/6537
:::

This is how I would do it in regular LaTeX (though I would use `\[...\]` to enclose display math):

```latex
$$\mathbf{I}_n = \left.\left( 
                  \vphantom{\begin{array}{c}1\\1\\1\\1\\1\end{array}}
                  \smash{\underbrace{
                      \begin{array}{ccccc}
                             1&0&0&\cdots &0\\
                             0&1&0&\cdots &0\\
                             0&0&1&\cdots &0\\
                             \vdots&&&\ddots&\\
                             0&0&0&\cdots &1
                      \end{array}
                      }_{n\text{ columns}}}
              \right)\right\}
              \,n\text{ rows}
$$
```

The `\vphantom` line creates a box whose height is equal to an nx1 array of 1's.  The `\smash` around your matrix typesets the matrix (including the underbrace) but makes its height and depth zero.  Put these together and you have a box which includes the underbrace, but whose width and height are equal to that of the matrix without the underbrace.  

![sample code output][1]

See ["A complement to `\smash`, `\llap`, and `\rlap`" by Alexander R. Perlis in *TUGBoat*][3] for more on all of these commands and also `\mathclap`.

I pasted it into the [MathJax demo page][2] too and it seems to work.


  [1]: tYwZG.png
  [2]: http://www.mathjax.org/demos/
  [3]: http://math.arizona.edu/~aprl/publications/mathclap/perlis_mathclap_24Jun2003.pdf
